title: Track work inside possessions

blocks.text: A railway closes a line to trains only during **possessions**, agreed stretches of days, and track work on that line must lie wholly inside one possession. A line also takes one work gang at a time; gangs on different lines work independently. Days are numbered from 0.

Write `possession_plan(jobs, possessions)` in `possessions.py`. `jobs` maps a job to `(line, days)`; `possessions` maps a line to its possessions, each `(first_day, last_day)` with both days included. Return each job's start day, chosen so that the last job ends as early as possible. Every instance in the tests has a plan.

The model, with $`J`$ the jobs, $`\ell(j)`$ and $`d_j`$ each job's line and days, $`P_\ell`$ the possessions of line $`\ell`$, and $`L`$ the lines. A job fits in possession $`(f, l)`$ when it starts on a day from $`f`$ to $`l - d_j + 1`$:
Build each start's domain with `cp_model.Domain.from_intervals`, whose ranges include both ends. The tests check the plan you return and how early it ends. About twenty lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model


def possession_plan(jobs: dict[str, tuple[str, int]], possessions: dict[str, list[tuple[int, int]]]) -> dict[str, int]:
    """Start day of each job, inside one possession of its line, so the last ends as early as possible."""
    horizon = max(last + 1 for spans in possessions.values() for _, last in spans)
    model = cp_model.CpModel()
    start, on_line = {}, {}
    for name, (line, days) in jobs.items():
        ranges = [[first, last - days + 1] for first, last in possessions[line] if last - days + 1 >= first]
        start[name] = model.new_int_var_from_domain(cp_model.Domain.from_intervals(ranges), f"start_{name}")
        on_line.setdefault(line, []).append(model.new_fixed_size_interval_var(start[name], days, f"work_{name}"))
    for intervals in on_line.values():
        model.add_no_overlap(intervals)

    makespan = model.new_int_var(0, horizon, "makespan")
    model.add_max_equality(makespan, [start[name] + days for name, (_, days) in jobs.items()])
    model.minimize(makespan)
    solver = cp_model.CpSolver()
    solver.parameters.num_workers = 1
    solver.solve(model)
    return {name: solver.value(start[name]) for name in jobs}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(possession_plan({"rails": ("north", 3), "points": ("north", 2), "drain": ("south", 4)},
                          {"north": [(0, 3), (8, 12)], "south": [(2, 9)]}))

possessions = {"up": [(0, 2), (6, 11)], "down": [(4, 8)]}

cases.says: jobs on different lines, each with room in an early possession, all start on its first day
every job gets a whole-number start day
a job lies wholly inside one possession of its line, so a job that does not fit in what is left of one waits for the next
two jobs on the same line never run on the same day
